items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: With Russell Ferrante I might — I often will send a little phone memo... we’ve known each other for 35 years now... Russell arranged it for me.

ctx.x: So how does that come about? When you have a song like this and you write the lyrics, are you already singing it and establishing a melody when you get together with a pianist that you have for them, and you’re going to sing it to them? Is that a fair assessment?

Well it doesn’t work that way exactly. I used to write lyrics to existing music at the beginning — old music, Fats Waller, Duke Ellington. That’s what I did for several albums. And then when I started writing with the living it changed. What I do is, I © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

almost always I come up with a lyric idea first and I bring it to them. It’s a little different with every guy. With Russell Ferrante I might — I often will send a little phone memo of me speaking to a metronome the phrasing to the whole song. But it’s just — it’s different with everybody. But usually, like with Eddie, he’s — Russell is a virtuosic pianist of course. Eddie is a great guitar player but we usually write on piano. So it used to be that I would always go over to his home studio and he would say,…
